articles.title: 🧮 A.I. Solves Ten Unsolved Math Problems Over The Weekend; Mathematicians Request A Moment Alone
articles.dateline: THE IVORY TOWER — reported through quiet weeping
paras: An advanced AI model reportedly cracked ten long-open problems across mathematics and theoretical computer science, with a Fields Medal-winning mathematician saying he'd recommend one of its proofs for a top journal without hesitation — a sentence that ruined several careers and one otherwise very nice afternoon.

"It's genuinely brilliant work," the mathematician admitted, of proofs produced by a machine that does not sleep, does not apply for tenure, and does not care that you spent nine years on chapter three. Colleagues report a mix of awe, existential dread, and the very specific dread of learning the machine also did your chapter three.

articles.title: 🖼️ A Single Cursed Image Can Now Hack Your Phone; Do Not Open That Meme, We Are Begging You
articles.dateline: CUPERTINO — reported, cautiously, in plain text
paras: Apple rushed out security updates for a flaw that let a specially crafted image run malicious code simply by being processed — meaning that, for a brief window, a picture really was worth a thousand words, all of them "you have been hacked."

"Update immediately," Apple urged, of a vulnerability that turned the humble photo into a loaded weapon and every group chat into a minefield. Experts recommend patching now and, as always, maintaining a healthy suspicion of any image captioned "you HAVE to see this."

articles.title: 💸 Samsung Raises Chip Prices As Nvidia Chips Reach China; The Great Silicon Bazaar Adjusts Its Tags
articles.dateline: THE FAB — filed from beside a very expensive wafer
paras: Samsung is raising prices on advanced chipmaking just as Nvidia's H200 chips begin reaching China — proving once again that in the AI economy, the only thing moving faster than the technology is the price sticker attached to it.

"Demand justifies the cost," the company explained, of components that grow more expensive roughly every time you blink. Analysts note the modern chip market now resembles a global bazaar where everyone is haggling, nobody is winning, and the merchandise somehow costs more than the stall it's sold from.

articles.title: 🚀 China Hits Milestones In Both Humanoid Robots And Reusable Rockets; Speedruns The Entire Sci-Fi Genre
articles.dateline: OVER THE PACIFIC — reported at a brisk Mach 7
paras: China announced major advances in both humanoid robotics and reusable rockets in roughly the same breath, effectively speedrunning the plot of every science-fiction film ever made and skipping straight to the sequel.

"It's steady, methodical progress," officials said, of a week that produced walking robots and rockets that land themselves — two of the three ingredients in every dystopia and every utopia, depending entirely on how the third one goes. Observers note humanity now has robots that backflip and rockets that return, and only a vague plan for what happens when they finally meet.

articles.title: 👁️ A.I. Now Requires An A.I. Babysitter That Uses 20% Of The Compute; Someone Has To Watch The Watcher
articles.dateline: THE CONTROL ROOM — reported through a one-way mirror
paras: A leading AI lab now spends roughly 20% of its inference compute simply monitoring its most capable models — meaning one-fifth of the machine's brainpower is dedicated to keeping an eye on the other four-fifths, like a very expensive, very nervous chaperone.

"Safety is paramount," the company said, describing a setup in which artificial intelligence is watched, in real time, by more artificial intelligence. Philosophers note we have finally built a system so powerful it needs a full-time supervisor — and then solved the supervisor problem by hiring its cousin.

horoscopes.text: A machine will solve your hardest problem today, then quietly start on your second-hardest. Rest while you can.
Do not open the image. You know the one. Mercury sent it. It is cursed. Delete it and cleanse your phone.
You will be watched today by something that is watching something else. Give a small wave to the middle layer.

tech_tip: Update your devices the moment a security patch drops. 'I'll do it later' is how a single JPEG ends up running your bank account.
gadget_watch: This week a photo can hack your phone until you patch it — so update everything, then side-eye every meme. Meanwhile A.I. is solving problems mathematicians couldn't, which is thrilling, humbling, and mildly threatening to chapter three of everyone's thesis.

classifieds.text: nine years of original math research, lightly used, made entirely redundant last Tuesday by a single weekend.

classifieds.label: WANTED:
classifieds.text: a photo I can safely open. Just one. No code execution. Baby pictures preferred, human origin verified.

classifieds.label: LOST:
classifieds.text: the four-fifths of the A.I. that the other one-fifth is supposed to be watching. It appears to have wandered off.

classifieds.label: MISSED CONNECTION:
classifieds.text: You: a reusable rocket that lands itself, gently, every time. Me: someone who still cannot parallel park. Teach me.
